newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia army to continue pullout, rebels stall.
newsitem.headline: Colombia army to continue pullout, rebels stall.

text.p: The army will press ahead with the demilitarization of sections of southern jungle, Colombia's defence chief said on Sunday, despite leftist rebels' refusal to honour a request to hand over 60 captured soldiers.

Last week, President Ernesto Samper ordered the army to pull troops out of 5,400 square miles (14,000 sq km) of Caqueta province for 10 days starting Dec. 6, offering the pullout in exchange for the release of the captured troops.
But in a communique on Saturday, the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rejected the offer on the grounds that barracks in towns within the demilitarized zone would still be manned.

Defence Minister Juan Carlos Esguerra condemned the rebel demands for a wider area to be cleared to make way for the handover of the troops, seized when guerrillas overran a base in neighbouring Putumayo province on Aug. 30.

"The government decision was an offer of good faith to break the deadlock. Sadly the FARC is not acting in good faith," Esguerra told Reuters. "The demilitarization of the zone will continue, however, and we hope the guerrilla will realise our offer really is very generous."
The capture of the troops, in an attack that marked the start of one of the bloodiest guerrilla offensives in three decades of armed uprising, was a humiliating blow for the army.

Until Samper's announcement last week, the military high command resisted any move that would have been seen as bowing to the rebel demands. Esguerra said on Sunday the government would not cede another inch to the guerrillas and said there could be no question of evacuating military bases within the demilitarized zone.

The army has denied claims it was preparing to rescue the soldiers by force. But Esguerra did not rule this out as a possible last resort on Sunday, saying simply he did not know whether it was a viable option.
Samper is due to hold a crisis meeting with defence and army chiefs on Monday to discuss the implications of the rebels' rejection of the government terms for the soldiers' release.
